title: 英語　和訳・説明問題
subtitle: 試験対策｜下線部和訳・内容説明
subject: english
instructions: 解答は、結論だけでなく、考え方の過程（論理・式・根拠）が採点者に伝わるように記述しなさい。
部分点は採点基準に示した観点ごとに与える。

stimuli.content:
Most of us try hard to avoid failure. (1) [[u:It is often not failure itself that we fear, but how others see us when we fail.]] As a result, many people choose easy tasks that they are sure to complete, rather than difficult ones from which they could learn more.

However, some educators argue that we should (2) [[u:treat failure as information]]. When an experiment does not work, a scientist does not decide that she is a bad scientist. Instead, she sees the result as a sign of what to try next.

In one study, students who were taught to think of mistakes as part of learning worked longer on difficult problems than students who were not, and in the end they achieved higher scores. The lesson is clear: if we can stop worrying about how we look, failure can become one of our best teachers.
stimuli.title: 次の英文を読んで、あとの問いに答えなさい。

questions.stem: 下線部 (1) を日本語に訳しなさい。

answer.value: 私たちが失敗を恐れるのは、失敗そのものが危険だからではなく、他人に自分がどう見られるかを気にするからであることが多い。

rubric.criterion: 強調構文（not A but B）を正しく訳している

questions.stem: 本文の主張に対するあなたの考えを、80 語程度の英語で書きなさい。

answer.value: I agree with the writer. When I failed my first speech contest, I felt embarrassed, but my teacher told me to think about what went wrong. I realized that I had spoken too fast, so I practiced speaking slowly. In the next contest, I won second prize. This experience taught me that failure can be a useful guide. If we stop worrying about how others see us, we can learn much more from our mistakes.
